describe.submission: a directory; see readme for its required contents
describe.readme:
# CPU kernel optimization

Make single-threaded matrix multiplication faster in C while keeping its answers correct. This hill measures CPU throughput in GFLOP/s; higher is better.

**First run:** choose **Climb on AutoLab**. The starter runs on CPU. Official scoring needs private evaluation data that is omitted from the public local download.

![Blocked matrix multiply: the road from naive loops to cache-aware tiles](assets/hero.svg)

## Run the starter

The starter in `examples/baseline/` is a straightforward three-loop matrix
multiply. Use its result on your own machine as the baseline. There is no single
expected speed for every CPU: five unchanged starter runs at `n=512` on the
review Mac ranged from **3.74 to 3.81 GFLOP/s**, with a median of about **3.75**.
That is a measurement example, not a target for another machine.

On AutoLab, click **Start a climb**, then **Climb on AutoLab**. Choose an agent
model and either a connected CPU machine or **CPU only (small)**. Set a model
budget under **More options**. AutoLab copies `kernel.c` into the climb. Check
that its baseline passes before reviewing changes; pause when you want to stop.

The evaluator needs Python 3.11 or newer, NumPy, and a C compiler available as
`cc`. Its environment installs NumPy; the machine must already have the compiler.
The starter is intended for Linux or macOS with GCC or Clang. No GPU is needed.
`cc --version` checks whether the compiler is available.

## Compute and cost

The agent model writes experiments; the compute runs them. The model budget covers model calls. Rented compute is billed separately. Pause the climb to stop experiments and release AutoLab rentals; your own connected machine remains yours to manage.

Before changing anything, open the baseline job and check for a passing score. **Nodes offline** means compute is disconnected, not that your solution failed.

## Try a first change

On AutoLab, ask the agent to make this edit in your submission, then run one evaluation against the baseline.

The starter loops over `i`, then `j`, then `k`. Try `i`, then `k`, then `j`, so
the innermost loop walks contiguous rows of B and C. Initialize each output row
before accumulating into it:

```c
void gemm(int n, const float *A, const float *B, float *C) {
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        for (int j = 0; j < n; j++) C[i * n + j] = 0.0f;
        for (int k = 0; k < n; k++) {
            float a = A[i * n + k];
            for (int j = 0; j < n; j++)
                C[i * n + j] += a * B[k * n + j];
        }
    }
}
```

Evaluate with the same size, tolerance and machine. Check correctness first,
then compare throughput and the three durations in `details.timings_seconds`.
Repeat close results: a small change within timing variation is not convincing
progress. After loop order, try blocking, vectorization or unrolling.

## What to submit

Submit a directory containing a self-contained `kernel.c` with this function:

```c
void gemm(int n, const float *A, const float *B, float *C);
```

Compute `C = A @ B` for row-major `n x n` float32 matrices. You may change the
algorithm and C implementation. Use one thread, no external libraries, and no
BLAS calls. Keep the evaluator, correctness inputs and compiler flags unchanged.

## Scoring and timing

The compiler command uses `cc -O3 -march=native -ffast-math -shared -fPIC`, with
`-lm` linked. Correctness is checked against NumPy on private seeded inputs,
including fresh inputs for every timed repetition. A no-op at the timed size
or a cached answer from warmup does not pass those checks.

After warmup, the evaluator times three calls at `n=512`. Each timed call
includes output allocation and zeroing plus the Python/ctypes call overhead;
input generation and NumPy verification are outside the timed section.

**`gflops = 2 * n^3 / seconds_best_of_3 / 1e9`.** The score keeps the existing
best-of-three convention. The report also includes all three durations, compiler
version and flags, operating system and architecture so you can inspect the
measurement. These details do not make different machines comparable.

A failed result explains a compilation or correctness problem in `details.error`.
Fix it before comparing speed. Correctness errors identify the case or timed
repetition without revealing the private seed.

## Local work

The public download does not include the private seeds needed for official
scoring. You can write and compile the kernel locally, but **use AutoLab for
scored runs with the public version**. A separate public practice evaluation is
not provided yet.

With an authorized complete hill bundle, run from the folder containing
`.autolab/`, using a fresh `my-kernel` folder:

```sh
cp -R .autolab/hills/kernel-opt/examples/baseline ./my-kernel
hills eval ./my-kernel -H kernel-opt -o baseline.json
```

Local results are not automatically added to AutoLab's leaderboard.

## Other settings

| Parameter | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `n` | 512 | Timed square matrix size |
| `tolerance` | `2e-3` | Maximum relative error against the NumPy result |

The relative error is the largest absolute output error divided by the largest
absolute reference value, with `1e-9` added to the denominator. Results compare
only within the same machine name, size, tolerance and evaluation mode. Keep
other workloads off the CPU when measuring. Evaluation runs are serialized on
the machine by this hill's CPU exclusivity setting.

`--final` uses a separate private correctness seed set and records a separate
comparison group. Keep reports unedited; `hills verify` checks their signatures
with the matching signing key.

## Trust

This is a cooperative performance exercise. Do not read private seeds, cache
answers across calls, or bypass the one-thread rule. Correctness checks are not
a sandbox: submission code and evaluation currently run as the same
operating-system user on AutoLab.

## If the first run fails

- **Compiler missing:** run `cc --version` on the machine doing the evaluation. Choose a CPU machine with GCC or Clang installed.
- **Compilation error:** open the failed job's logs and check the first compiler error and the required `gemm` signature.
- **Incorrect answer:** check that every output entry is initialized and that rows use `i * n + j` indexing.
- **Missing private inputs locally:** use **Climb on AutoLab** for official scoring. The public download supports editing and compilation only.

Run the baseline on the machine you will optimize on. A faster CPU alone is not evidence that your code improved. This hill runs C on a CPU; CUDA kernels belong in a separate GPU benchmark.

## Versions and comparisons

A climb stays on the hill version selected when it was created. To try a newly published version, start a new climb from the hill page. Old results stay with their original version, including when a new version only changes this README.
